question: Does the navigating agent's learned memory carry over to larger planted not-all-equal patterns when its long-horizon reads count no steps, when it trains on patterns of 3,200 distinctions, both, or neither?
inputs: WHERE-NEXT's local reads; for flag 16, ages read relative to the attended knot's oldest distinction and to the oldest candidate, the violated fraction in the recurrent input.
forbidden_inputs: The hidden planted state, any test instance during training, validation or tuning, and any solver output.
mapping: The WHERE-NEXT policy (326 weights) trained by OpenAI-ES; arms L3s, L3m, L3sm, L2m and L3c, two seeds each, both tested.
primary_observable: Per arm, R = geometric mean of the two seeds' median flips / median flips of the best re-tuned hand-written rule on rand at 4 times its largest training size, 99% paired bootstrap; ratios S, T, C, I, K between arms.
comparators_or_controls: WHERE-NEXT's hand-written rules (reused run for run, gate G6) and Novelty+ and sticky re-tuned at 51200; WHERE-NEXT's L3 (both seeds); the schedule control L3c and the memoryless L2m.
resource_budget: Ten ES trainings (about 25 CPU-hours) and test cells to rand n = 51200, CPU only, MemoryMax 16G under the shared runner.
first_executable_signal: Gate G including G6 (run-for-run identity with WHERE-NEXT's engine); then G-learn and G-train per arm.
stop_rule: Stop at the frozen decision rule and diagnosis; keep every run, failed or censored.
nonclaims: Planted instances only; no general SAT method; no claim about unrestricted solvers, P vs NP, native emergence or self-improving AI; knot structures fixed.
